review.notes: Triage review of all 73 physical pages: full-document automated diff (normalized 4-gram containment plus normalized line-presence per page), then line-by-line inspection of every low-containment page (contributor list pages 47-61, evaluation tables on 11 and 13-16, appendix tables on 63-65, references on 41-46, chart pages 16 and 72). Structural scan found zero code fences, so no swallowed-content risk; the only spurious heading is repaired by patch 1. The 17 contributor-list repairs were each verified on a 300-dpi render of the printed name (pages 47, 49, 50, 51, 52, 53, 55, 56, 59); the page-break sentence merge was verified on a full 150-dpi render of physical pages 26-27, which print the sentence as running body text. Missing lines on chart pages 11, 16 and 72 are axis labels and milestone labels inside embedded figures, not defects; 'Ofir Roval', 'Nate Kushman'/'Blair Kutzman' and the apostrophe names (O'Brien, D'Souza, ...) match the print's own spellings and were left unchanged. Contributor prose flow on pages 47-61 was machine-scanned for drops but not manually read name by name beyond the automated diff.

unresolved.evidence: The contributor pages 47-61 are typeset in multi-column name lists; OCR emits prose blocks and HTML tables whose local order does not always match the printed column order, and the automated line-presence diff cannot distinguish reordering from drops for names that DO appear. The line-level sweep found no name string missing outright after the repairs above, but a manual name-by-name read of all ~3400 entries was out of triage scope. Scattered single-diacritic drops (e.g. 'Raia Hadsell' area, 'Alejo n' style artifacts not checked) may remain.

The OCR table element before the 'Table 4 |' caption contains, after the Image Understanding rows, a second header row ('Benchmark / Gemini 1.5 Flash / ... / GPT 4o transcribe') plus FLEURS and CoVoST2 audio rows that belong to Table 5; the two printed tables appear merged into one HTML <table>. Restructuring table boundaries is a layout-level repair that needs the exporter's table handling reviewed before changing recorded values.
